CITY OF PASADENA
  City Council Minutes
  June 29, 2020 - 2:00 P.M.
  City Hall Council Chamber

  SPECIAL MEETING
  The virtual meeting was convened pursuant to Executive Order N-29-20 issued by
  Governor Gavin Newsom on March 17, 2020, and was held solely by
  videoconference/teleconference

OPENING:  Mayor Tomek called the special meeting to order at 2:03 p.m. The
  pledge of allegiance was led by Councilmember Madison.

CONSENT CALENDAR  AUTHORIZATION TO ENTER INTO A CONTRACT WITH ST.

  SERVICES FOR A TERM OF THREE YEARS OR UNTIL
  $600,000 IS EXPENDED, WHICHEVER OCCURS FIRST
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1) Find that the action proposed in the agenda report is not a
  "project" as defined in the California Environmental Quality Act
  (CEQA), Public Resources Code Section 21065 and Section
  15378(b)(2) of the State CEQA Guidelines and, as such, is not
  subject to environmental review; and
  (2)  Authorize the City Manager to enter into a contract with St.
  George's Medical Clinic following a competitive selection process
  pursuant to Pasadena Municipal Code Section 4.08.047, for pre-
  employment medical review and physicals, OSHA mandated
  physicals and medical monitoring, occupational therapy, and drug
  screens for a term of three years or in an amount not-to-exceed
  $600,000, whichever occurs first. Competitive Bidding is not
  required pursuant to City Charter Section 1002(F), Contracts for
  Professional or Unique Services. (Contract No. 31758)

REPORTS AND COMMENTS  HOTEL WORKER PROTECTIONS
FROM COUNCIL  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council
COMMITTEES  receive the following report and consider whether to direct any
  further action.

  City Manager Mermell provided introductory comments, and Eric
  Duyshart, Businesses Development Administrator, presented a
  PowerPoint presentation on the item, and responded to questions.

  Councilmember Gordo, Chair of the Economic Development and
  Technology (EDTech) Committee, reported that the Committee
  voted to forward this item to the City Council for consideration; and
  asked staff to provide additional information on the ownership
  groups of the hotels in the City. He spoke in support of a hotel
  worker protection ordinance.

  Councilmember Kennedy expressed concerns with the lack of
  effort to obtain data from hotel employees. He spoke in favor of
  staff developing a fair ordinance, which states that hotels that were
  affected by the COVID-19 pandemic, and were required to lay off
  employees, should be required to provide those employees with
  an opportunity to return to their jobs. He also spoke in favor of the
  City adopting an ordinance similar to the Los Angeles County's,
  Right of Recall ordinance.

Council Minutes  3  06/29/2020
   Councilmember Madison spoke on surrounding cities that have
  adopted Hotel Worker protection ordinances; and expressed his
  disappointment on the lack of information on legal challenges and
  rulings related to hotel worker protections. He spoke in favor of
  directing staff to develop a hotel worker protection ordinance for
  hotels with 50 or more rooms.

  Javan Rad, Chief Assistant City Attorney, provided information on
  worker protection laws, and responded to questions.

  Councilmember Wilson spoke on the need for staff to clarify that if
  the City adopts an ordinance, the ordinance does not mandate
  that hotels will re-open and reinstate hotel jobs immediately; and
  expressed concerns with expanding the City's scope of authority
  into areas that may not be permissible.

  Councilmember Masuda spoke on the need for staff to determine
  why hotel operators are being singled out for worker protections.
  He expressed concerns with forcing hotels to abide by worker
  retention regulations as California is an at-will employment state.

  City Manager Mermell summarized past City Council and EDTech
  Committee discussions on the item, with those discussions
  providing the reasons for the focus on the hospitality industry, and
  specifically hotels, and responded to questions.

  Councilmember McAustin sympathized with hospitality workers
  during this difficult time, however, expressed concerns with City
  government inserting itself between labor and management.

  Vice Mayor Hampton stated that hoteliers pay Transient
  Occupancy Tax fees, which is a return on the City's investment.
  He spoke in favor of an ordinance for hotel worker protections that
  includes a sunset date related to the end of the COVID-19
  pandemic.

  City Clerk Jomsky reported that 456 letters in support and 1 letter
  expressing opposition of hotel worker protections were received,
  distributed to the City Council, posted on-line, and made part of
  the public record. The following comments were read aloud,

Council Minutes  5  06/29/2020
   City Clerk Jomsky also read aloud comments expressing
  concerns with the City adopting an ordinance on hotel worker
  protections, from the following individuals:

  Siamak Nassirpour, representing The Westin Pasadena
  Paul Little, representing Pasadena Chamber of Commerce
  Aline, Pasadena resident

  Councilmember Madison informed the City Council that on June
  16, 2020, the City of Glendale, CA, adopted similar Hospitality
  Worker protections.

  Vice Mayor Hampton requested that the direction to staff include
  a report back to the City Council with an update 12 months after
  the COVID-19 emergency order is lifted.

  Councilmember Wilson expressed sympathy to low wage earners
  who are economically impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic,
  however, he struggles with singling out one component of the
  City's economy. He stated that he does not believe this action is
  within the purview of municipal affairs to be employment arbiters,
  and therefore is unable to support the motion.

  Mayor Tomek expressed concerns similar to those of
  Councilmembers McAustin, Masuda and Wilson regarding the
  City inserting itself between labor and management groups,
  however, he stated his support for the motion. He disclosed that
  he has met with hoteliers, representatives of UNITE HERE Local
  11, and hotel workers to discuss hotel worker protections.

  Following discussion, it was moved by Councilmember Madison,
  seconded by Councilmember Kennedy, to direct staff to prepare
  an ordinance securing the Right of Recall, Worker Retention, and
  Private Right of Action, applicable to hotels of 50 rooms or more,
  with staff to return to the City Council with a report on the efficacy
  of the Ordinance, 12 months after the COVID-19 emergency order
  is lifted:

  AYES:  Councilmembers Gordo, Kennedy, Madison, Vice
  Mayor Hampton, Mayor Tomek
  NOES:  Councilmembers Masuda, Wilson
  ABSENT: None
  ABSTAIN: Councilmember McAustin

  Mayor Tomek, Chair of the Finance Committee, reported on the
  Committee's meeting and summarized the discussion on the
  City's updated detailed COVID-19 pandemic impact report,
  accuracy of income projections; and that the Committee asked
  staff to restate how the City allocates both General and Non-
  General funds. He also reported, as Chair of the Legislative Policy
  Committee, that the Committee discussed a package of housing

Council Minutes  6  06/29/2020
   bills that if adopted, will have far reaching ramifications to the City.
  He stated that the Committee will continue to track and monitor
  these bills and report back to the City Council. He congratulated
  the Rose Bowl Operating Company for organizing the upcoming
  virtual AmericaFest 4th of July Celebration; and spoke on the need
  for the community to continue to practice social distancing due to
  COVID-19 pandemic.

  Councilmember Gordo requested that the City Council begin
  preparations for revenue losses, so that the City is prepared to
  make difficult decisions in terms of services and staffing, which
  also involves difficult discussions with collective bargaining units;
  and asked that staff provide a comparative analysis on the
  differences in Emergency Health Orders between the City of Los
  Angeles, County of Los Angeles, and City of Long Beach.

  Councilmember McAustin, Chair of the Municipal Services
  Committee, reported that the Committee reviewed some of the
  changes underway at Pasadena Transit due to the COVID-19
  pandemic; and held a discussion on additional testing by the City
  at the Power Plant to comply with insurance requirements.

  Councilmember Kennedy, Chair of the Public Safety Committee,
  reported on the efforts of the Fire and Police Departments as they
  work to curtail illegal fireworks in the City; discussion on the
  consideration of civilian police oversight model and the
  development of the framework of such a model with the Mayor,
  and with input from a number of experts from the City; and
  responded to questions.

  City Manager Mermell provided a brief update on the State's
  closures of bars in various counties due to elevated COVID-19
  case rates; and responded to questions.

  Councilmember Gordo, Chair of the Economic Development and
  Technology Committee, stated the Committee continues to
  monitor the re-opening of local businesses in the City.

  Vice Mayor Hampton spoke on the need to engage various City
  departments to assist with the prevention of illegal fireworks in the
  City, and thanked the Pasadena Fire and Police Departments for
  their work in patrolling and attempting to stop the use of illegal
  fireworks in the City.

  City Clerk Jomsky reported on the number of Census self-
  response rates of 64% in the City and encouraged the public to
  log onto: www.my2020cenus.gov to complete the 2020 Census.
